title: October 23 — Confusing Friday: visual binding, missing information and a ghost
summary: Complements the separate October 23 BindingClaude/BindingSol/WhiteBox source pass with SihtiGraphModel, DoDis and GhostYou. Image-specific Walsh/relational distillation is measured on two correctly classified CIFAR birds, with retention-conditioned gains and failure at severe masking and no stable cross-bird tile mapping. DoDis v1 replaces hidden multiscale pieces from memory and gets small image-MSE improvement against a strong shuffled-binding comparator; classifier guidance improves margin while worsening image fidelity. DoDis v2 implements local cross-scale addresses and publishes a large 100-bird results folder, but its full aggregate was not verified for this atlas addition. GhostYou is a finished playful, browser-local webcam and audio sketch rather than a model result. The common research question is whether visible context can address unseen detail; nothing here establishes a general image generator or true network-internal circuit.

nodes.claim: Train a small CIFAR-10 CNN, decompose one 32x32 image into 64 additive scale-and-tile switches and extract a sparse behavioral interaction graph for that fixed image's masked-input logit margin; v2 directly tests single/pair relations and v3 stratifies by the fraction of original pieces retained.
nodes.survived: Source-saved v3: on bird #65, the mixture graph has held-out R² 0.666 (90% retained) and 0.635 (95%); bird #70 independently refitted yields 0.851 and 0.882. The p=.90-only graph reaches R² 0.839/0.886 on bird #65 at p=.90/.95, and 0.864/0.918 on #70. These beat the frozen v2 graph under mostly-intact masks on #65; distinct local fits show the query/readout mechanism is workable.
nodes.killed: Original v1 preregistered graph gates fail; v2 mean-fill global graph reaches R² 0.534 at p=.50 but falls to -3.035 at p=.90. v3 bird #65 mixture misses the p=.50 R²>=.35 gate (0.295), and the p=.90-only graph falls to -3.372 at p=.50. Bird #70 is refit separately, not cross-image transfer; the learned same-tile B0×B3 links have 0 shared tiles across birds. Input mask effects are not recovered internal CNN circuitry or missing-image generation.
nodes.era: October 23: image-specific relation explanations are sensitive to what remains visible

nodes.claim: Combines an explicit source of actual missing pixel content (donor image memory), learned local/cross-band consistency graph and optionally a frozen-CNN purpose surrogate; accepts only energy-decreasing local piece replacements. V2 adds context-addressed local donor retrieval instead of relying on whole-image nearest-neighbor donors.
nodes.survived: On 12 held-out CIFAR birds with 50% multiscale pieces hidden, v1 learned binding cuts mean pixel MSE from 0.01494 memory+seams to 0.01417 (9/12 improved). The classifier-purpose term raises actual bird margin from -0.003 to +1.578 with shared choices. V2 code/protocol defines 100 selected fresh birds, seven matched baselines and per-piece visible-context addresses; 100 per-bird receipts and a large results.json exist in runs/v2_local_100_birds on main.
nodes.killed: Shuffling the learned graph still obtains 0.01438 pixel MSE, capturing most of the improvement against 0.01494: the learned advantage over shuffled is only about 0.00021 on 12 birds, not compelling visual grammar. CNN-purpose increases MSE from 0.01417 to 0.01482 while increasing classifier margin. V1 patches have Frankenstein-like donor artifacts; 32x32 multiscale masking is not natural rectangular inpainting. V2 aggregate outcome was not independently parsed for this pass, and its README still claims no completed v2 CIFAR result: no v2 success verdict is inferred from committed files.
nodes.era: October 23: incomplete information starts functioning as an address

nodes.claim: An independent Halloween browser toy uses webcam background calibration and motion to make a moving person transparent and map vertical position and movement to a sine-wave theremin.
nodes.survived: A self-contained static HTML implementation and browser UI are published on GitHub Pages and Hugging Face Spaces. README describes a three-second empty-room capture, webcam-local processing and motion-controlled audio.
nodes.killed: No independent live browser/device acceptance test or video-quality measurement was run for Genealogy; it is an expressive interactive sketch, not evidence for learned binding, generative vision or a new perceptual theory.

edges.why: SihtiGraphModel explicitly situates its mask-query Fourier search after the WhiteBox toy behavioral extractor, but moves from parity toys to one image and frozen CNN margin; no claim of direct code fork.
SihtiGraphModel explicitly names the Sihti family and implements additive octave/tile residues as external input coordinates for black-box CNN probing.
DoDis explicitly imports the 64-piece decomposition and frozen CNN/checkpoint from SihtiGraphModel, adding donor retrieval, graph scores and energy-based completion.
DoDis v2 explicitly revisits SihtiImageModel's notion of the coarse core as a partial address to local missing detail; this is a conceptual reuse of the memory-query question.

motifs.title: An image-specific explanation changes with which fragments remain visible
motifs.description: SihtiGraphModel extracts useful sparse input-switch dependencies for a frozen classifier on two birds, but each bird is fit afresh, the learned tile links do not overlap, and uniform-mask success does not automatically extrapolate to nearly intact images or natural occlusions.

motifs.title: Incomplete visible context can act as an address into image memory
motifs.description: DoDis changes the problem from interpreting a frozen classifier to proposing actual missing residue content. The key candidate mechanism is local, cross-scale visible context choosing donors, with binding consistency as a separate filter. Its 12-bird first test leaves most binding gain explainable by a shuffled graph; the 100-bird local-address outcome still needs a complete numerical audit.

motifs.title: A research day can also end in a usable creative artifact
motifs.description: GhostYou is a standalone local-browser webcam/theremin Halloween toy; value comes from a runnable interaction, not from proving the day's relational-learning hypothesis.
